title: readScheduleState treats ANY read error (EBUSY/EACCES from an antivirus scan, ENOENT race) as ScheduleStateCorrupt, so a healthy file can be quarantined
evidence: The readFileSync and JSON.parse share one try/catch that throws ScheduleStateCorrupt. recordScheduled then renames the file aside and starts from an empty map. Bytes are kept, but dedup history leaves the live file. The tick's unlocked read self-heals (re-read under the lock); recordScheduled's read has no second chance.
fix_direction: Only a SyntaxError or non-object body is corruption; rethrow other fs errors (or retry briefly) without quarantining.

title: No test pins the lockStillOwned check before the schedule-state rename; a recordScheduled that writes after losing its lock passes every suite
evidence: A mutant replacing the owns() callback in recordScheduled with a no-op survived the schedule-state-safety, schedule-tick and schedule-state suites. Related note: an empty lock file left by a crash between create and write wedges dedup writes (each recordScheduled waits 5 s then fails, logged) until removed by hand; the tick still joins and re-creating the same task is idempotent.
fix_direction: Add a test that steals the lock between read and rename and expects nothing written.
